$schema: Context Window Explorer task graph — deep visualization platform for fractal agent context window telemetry
description: New Explorer tab in dashboard-local that reads fractal agent debug logs, builds a tree-aware invocation model, and renders per-node context window charts, a flame chart, run summary, and token flow sankey. Server-side extraction keeps the browser fast. Tree parser replaces the flat one with backward compat.
assumptions: dashboard-local Vite dev server is the target surface (not production build)
Real debug logs follow the cli-debug.log format with subagent_started/subagent_completed markers
d3-sankey npm package is available and compatible with the project's ESM setup
Existing Logs tab consumers must not break (flattenTree backward compat)
SVG viewBox manipulation provides crisp zoom without CSS transform scaling

designDecisions.rationale: Recharts Sankey is basic and poorly documented. d3-sankey gives full control over layout, link styling, and node positioning.

designDecisions.decision: SVG viewBox for zoom instead of CSS transform
designDecisions.rationale: CSS transform: scale() loses resolution. ViewBox manipulation keeps SVG paths crisp at any zoom level.
Most controllable for custom time-block rendering with depth-based stacking. No existing chart library has a flame chart component.

designDecisions.decision: Server-side extraction instead of client-side parsing
designDecisions.rationale: 1M line / ~150MB logs cannot be loaded into browser memory. Server extracts only telemetry events (~KB) and returns structured JSON.

designDecisions.decision: Rewrite parser with flattenTree() adapter over parallel new parser
designDecisions.rationale: Single source of truth for subagent parsing. flattenTree() provides backward compat for existing Logs tab with zero behavioral change.

designDecisions.decision: Basic path traversal prevention (resolve + check canonical form + .log extension) over allowlist
designDecisions.rationale: This is a local dev tool. Basic validation prevents accidental misuse without over-engineering.

tasks.title: Define SubagentTreeNode, ParsedTree, and RunSummary types
tasks.description: Add new tree-aware type interfaces to tool-timeline-types.ts — SubagentTreeNode (extends SubagentSpan fields with tree structure), ParsedTree (root + allNodes), RunSummary + AgentBreakdownEntry (aggregate stats).
acceptanceCriteria: SubagentTreeNode interface exported with id, depth, parentId, children, invocationIndex, contextWindowEntries, assistantUsageEntries fields
ParsedTree interface exported with root and allNodes fields
RunSummary and AgentBreakdownEntry interfaces exported
npm run lint passes with no errors

tasks.title: Rewrite parser as parseCliDebugTree()
tasks.description: Replace the flat single-currentSpan parser with a stack-based tree builder. Returns ParsedTree with synthetic root node. Keeps old parseCliDebugSubagents() as a thin wrapper for backward compat.
acceptanceCriteria: parseCliDebugTree() exported and returns ParsedTree
Stack-based nesting: depth increments on subagent_started, decrements on subagent_completed
invocationIndex correctly counts per agent name (1-based)
Existing parseCliDebugSubagents() still works via delegation to tree parser + flatten

tasks.title: Add flattenTree() utility
tasks.description: DFS walk of SubagentTreeNode tree producing SubagentSpan[] for backward compat with existing Logs tab components. Skips synthetic root.
acceptanceCriteria: flattenTree() exported
Skips synthetic root (depth 0)
Returns SubagentSpan[] in DFS order
Output structurally compatible with old parseCliDebugSubagents() output

tasks.title: Refactor useToolTimelineData to use tree parser

acceptanceCriteria: useToolTimelineData uses parseCliDebugTree() + flattenTree()
subagentSpans output is identical to before
Existing Logs tab renders identically
npm run lint passes
